tweets.text: Google's Willow chip shrinks the ECDSA attack window to 9 minutes. Bitcoin's target block time? 10 minutes. The margin between 'safe' and 'cracked in the mempool' is now less than one block.
Caltech and Oratomic slashed the qubit count for cracking P-256 by 30x — down to 10,000 qubits. Their companion benchmark puts the secp256k1 attack window at 2027–2033. Not 'someday.' This decade.

33% of Bitcoin's total supply — roughly 6.9 million BTC — sits in addresses with exposed public keys today. The moment a cryptographically relevant quantum computer arrives, all of it is vulnerable. And the migration hasn't started.

Lightning's post-quantum math is brutal: replacing one ECC key requires THREE separate cryptosystems. Node announcements balloon from 140 bytes to 9,115. BOLT 11's max field literally can't fit a single PQ signature.
